delay tip dbdc:
Average the last <Delay Statistics> delay samples per online link (select 0 to disable the delay rule).
Three cases by parameters (excluded links may stay online, but are not used for load sharing):
1. <Delay Boundary(ms)> is 0:
	When to filter: always filter by gap to the best mean (no absolute boundary)
	Who joins balancing: links whose mean exceeds the best mean by no more than <Delay Difference(ms)>
2. <Delay Difference(ms)> is 0 (boundary non-zero):
	When to filter: among balancing online links, some means are below and some above the boundary; otherwise do not filter, all stay in balancing
	Who joins balancing: links whose mean is not above the boundary (any above the boundary are excluded)
3. Both boundary and difference non-zero:
	When to filter: among balancing online links, some means are below and some above the boundary; otherwise do not filter, all stay in balancing
	Who joins balancing:
		- Links whose mean is not above the boundary
		- Links whose mean is above the boundary, but that link's mean exceeds the best mean by no more than the difference
delay tip hot:
Average the last <Delay Statistics> delay samples per online link (select 0 to disable delay switching; then prefer smallest slot number only).
Switch rules:
	1. Among links with mean ≤ <Delay Boundary(ms)> (good-tier), prefer the smallest slot number.
	2. If the current link goes above the boundary, do not switch immediately; switch to the smallest-numbered good-tier link only when current exceeds that link's mean by more than <Delay Difference(ms)>.
	3. If there is no good-tier (all above boundary): pick the smallest-numbered among all online links.
	4. If the current link is offline: choose the target by the rules above and switch now.
delay tip lazy:
Average the last <Delay Statistics> delay samples per online link (select 0 to disable delay switching; while current link stays up and delay is off, do not fail back by slot number).
Current link offline: switch now (see switch target under each case).
Current link still up — three cases by parameters:
1. <Delay Boundary(ms)> is 0:
	When to switch: current link's mean exceeds the best mean by more than <Delay Difference(ms)>
	Switch target: lowest-mean online link
2. <Delay Difference(ms)> is 0 (boundary non-zero):
	When to switch: some online mean is below the boundary and current mean is above it
	Switch target: lowest-mean online link
3. Both boundary and difference non-zero:
	When to switch: all of the following
		- Some online link is below the boundary
		- Current mean is above the boundary
		- Current link's mean exceeds the best mean by more than the difference
	Switch target: lowest-mean online link
